A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a record of the most recent state of the database, even if the database itself is not up to date.
When a crash occurs, the database can use the log to recover to a consistent state. The database can read the log and apply the changes in the log to the database, effectively replaying the changes that were made before the crash. This ensures that the database is brought up to date, even if the database itself was not up to date at the time of the crash.
The write-ahead log also helps to prevent data loss in the event of a crash. If a change is made to the database and the database crashes before the change is written to the log, the change will be lost. However, if the change is written to the log but not to the database, the change will still be in the log and can be reapplied to the database when it is recovered. This ensures that all changes are preserved, even if the database crashes.
